marks.gloss_en: תניא כוותיה דשמואל: not on the wound, but outside it, and it flows down
the baraita like Shmuel: one does not put hot water and oil on a wound on Shabbat
שמע מינה -- from the distinction (new rags are forbidden on a wound) it follows that they heal
קשיא כתיתין אכתיתין! -- the baraita permits a dry pad and forbids dry rags
לא קשיא: הא בחדתי, הא בעתיקי -- the prohibition is of new rags, the permission of old ones (= p_ha_bechadtei, p_ha_beatikei)
the baraita: one puts on a wound a dry pad and a dry sponge
מיתיבי: one does not put oil and hot water on a pad to put on a wound on Shabbat -- against Rav
התם משום סחיטה -- there the prohibition is because of squeezing the pad (= p_hatam_sechita)
the baraita: one does not put oil and hot water on a pad to put on a wound on Shabbat
תא שמע: one does not put hot water and oil on a pad that is on a wound on Shabbat -- against Rav
התם נמי משום סחיטה -- there too, because of squeezing (= p_hatam_nami_sechita)
the baraita: one does not put hot water and oil on a pad that is on a wound on Shabbat
Rav: one does not withhold hot water and oil from a wound on Shabbat
"ערלתו" -- ערלתו ודאי דוחה את השבת: the baraita's derivation from the word
the baraita: his certain foreskin overrides Shabbat
the mishnah: a doubtful case and an androgynos -- one does not desecrate Shabbat for [circumcising] him
שנאמר: ויהי ביום השלישי בהיותם כואבים -- R' Elazar ben Azarya's verse for washing on the third day
the mishnah: one washes the baby both before the circumcision and after the circumcision
שנאמר: ויהי ביום השלישי בהיותם כואבים -- his verse for washing on the third day (kind svara stands in: no kind names a שנאמר derivation)
in the baraita: אף על פי שאין ראיה לדבר זכר לדבר, שנאמר... -- the same verse, graded as an allusion, not proof
תניא כוותיה דרבא: first day in his usual way; third day on Shabbat, sprinkle by hand
the baraita: one washes the baby before and after circumcision -- on the first day in his usual way
Rava: מתניתין כוותייהו דייקא -- the mishnah is precise according to Rav Yehuda and Rabba bar Avuh
והתניא כוותיה דמר? -- a baraita was taught in accordance with the Master; why regret?
מתניתין כוותייהו דייקא -- the mishnah's wording is precise according to them
ממאי -- from REBA's 'one washes': fitting if the first tanna said only 'sprinkle'; if the first tanna permits washing on the first day, REBA should have said 'ALSO washes' (אף מרחיצין מיבעי ליה)
והא אמרת רישא מרחיצין! -- if one may wash him, why only sprinkle by hand and not with a vessel?
Rav Yehuda and Rabba bar Avuh: it is taught as 'how?' -- the washing IS the sprinkling by hand (= p_keitzad_tani)
Rav Yehuda and Rabba bar Avuh: the mishnah is taught as 'how?' -- one washes the baby... how? one sprinkles on him by hand, not with a vessel
Rava: washing in the usual way is on the first day; sprinkling by hand only on the third day falling on Shabbat (= p_rava_hachi_katani)
והא מרחיצין קתני! -- the mishnah says 'one washes', and sprinkling is not washing

Rava: thus it teaches -- [one washes the baby before and after circumcision:] on the first day in his usual way, and on the third day that falls on Shabbat one sprinkles on him by hand, not with a vessel
וממאי דהכא בחמין שהוחמו בשבת פליגי? דילמא בחמין שהוחמו בערב שבת פליגי
Abaye: I wanted to answer him, but Rav Yosef answered first: because it is a danger for him (= p_sakana_lo)
because it is a danger for him [the baby]

if it were washing of the circumcision, is it worse than hot water on a wound? Rav said one does not withhold hot water and oil from a wound on Shabbat (= p_rav_ein_monin) -- so REBA would teach nothing
Rav: one does not withhold hot water and oil from a wound on Shabbat
the baraita: and when they sprinkle, they do not sprinkle with a cup, nor with a bowl, nor with a vessel, but by hand
[the stam:] why 'no proof, but an allusion'? because an adult's flesh does not heal quickly, a child's flesh heals quickly
a certain man came before Rava; he ruled for him according to his [Rava's] teaching
R' Elazar (via Rav Dimi): the halakha follows R' Elazar ben Azarya
R' Elazar ben Azarya's 'one washes' is washing of the whole body
Rav Yosef: is there no difference for you between hot water heated on Shabbat and hot water heated on Shabbat eve?
the halakha follows R' Elazar ben Azarya, whether with water heated on Shabbat or on Shabbat eve, whether washing the whole body or the circumcision -- because it is a danger for him
